claim_boundaries.basis: RAG benchmarks, long-context benchmarks, and domain RAG benchmarks are already abundant.
MultiHop-RAG, BRIDGE, MAGIC, and OCC-RAG make this crowded as a standalone claim.
ChronoQA, TEMPRAGEVAL, TDBench, and knowledge-drift work already cover temporal QA/RAG.
LongCite, step-context faithfulness, RAG faithfulness metrics, and FaithEval cover nearby citation/context faithfulness space.

claim_boundaries.claim: Unified hard-grounded research QA failure taxonomy beyond fact lookup
claim_boundaries.basis: Allowed only if the paper presents reviewed items spanning lifecycle, authority, stale/current snapshots, conclusion overreach, insufficiency, entity ambiguity, table/text, multi-hop, temporal, and contradiction categories.

claim_boundaries.claim: Paper-ready and genuinely novel as of June 2026
claim_boundaries.basis: Not allowed until human review, category scale, and final refreshed novelty audit are complete.

novelty_position: Plausibly differentiated only as a unified hard-grounded research QA failure taxonomy; not novel as generic RAG, citation, temporal, contradiction, or multi-hop QA.

sources.title: OCC-RAG: Optimal Cognitive Core for Faithful Question Answering
sources.gap: Optimizes context QA models and synthetic training data for multi-hop, faithfulness, and abstention, but does not organize evaluation around research-document lifecycle, authority, stale/current, citation-overreach, and temporal snapshot failure modes in one benchmark.

sources.title: ChronoQA: A Question Answering Dataset for Temporal-Sensitive Retrieval-Augmented Generation
covers: temporal questions: as of date X
sources.gap: Strong temporal RAG coverage, including multi-document temporal questions, but not a broad grounded-research taxonomy covering authority conflicts, appended document lifecycle, conclusion-support overreach, and abstention together.

sources.title: BRIDGE: Benchmark for multi-hop Reasoning In long multimodal Documents with Grounded Evidence
sources.gap: Covers long scientific documents and text/table/figure evidence, but focuses on multimodal multi-hop reasoning rather than stale/current conflicts, source authority, insufficiency, citation-overreach, entity ambiguity, and cross-document contradiction as a unified failure taxonomy.

sources.title: LIT-RAGBench: Benchmarking Generator Capabilities of Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.gap: Directly adjacent for insufficiency and contradiction, but smaller and aspect-based; it does not test document lifecycle, source authority hierarchy, as-of snapshot semantics, entity disambiguation, and citation support versus conclusion support in one large-corpus research QA suite.

sources.title: T2-RAGBench: Text-and-Table Benchmark for Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.gap: Directly pressures text-and-table RAG over finance documents, but does not cover source authority conflicts, stale/current document snapshots, appended lifecycle changes, evidence insufficiency, conclusion-overreach, or cross-document contradiction as a unified research QA taxonomy.

sources.title: Citation-Closure Retrieval and Per-Rule Attribution for Real-World Compliance RAG
sources.gap: Very close to authority-aware attribution, but targeted at regulatory rule closure rather than a benchmark taxonomy spanning lifecycle, temporal, insufficiency, entity ambiguity, and conclusion-support failure modes.

sources.title: Fine-grained Claim-level RAG Benchmark for Law
sources.gap: Covers claim-level legal RAG and contradiction detection, but domain scope and claim granularity differ from broad research-document QA with explicit source lifecycle and citation-overreach categories.

sources.title: EnterpriseRAG-Bench
sources.gap: Covers realistic large enterprise corpora, but is not organized around controlled hard-grounded failure classes such as stale/current conflicts, authority hierarchy, appended lifecycle changes, and citation-support versus conclusion-support.

sources.title: CorpusQA: A 10 Million Token Benchmark for Corpus-Level Question Answering
sources.gap: Tests corpus-scale synthesis difficulty, but does not isolate grounded research QA failure modes with per-item citation-support, authority, temporal, lifecycle, and contradiction rubrics.

sources.title: LongBench Pro: A More Realistic and Comprehensive Bilingual Long-Context Evaluation Benchmark
sources.gap: Strengthens the crowded long-context benchmark landscape, but does not directly target large-corpus grounded research QA with explicit evidence sufficiency and conclusion-support labels.

sources.title: LongCite / LongBench-Cite
sources.gap: Evaluates citation generation and correctness in long-context QA, but citation quality alone does not distinguish cases where a cited sentence supports a fact while failing to support the research conclusion.

sources.title: 100-LongBench: Are de facto Long-Context Benchmarks Literally Evaluating Long-Context Ability?
sources.gap: Targets long-context measurement validity, not grounded research QA failure categories or evidence-use semantics.

sources.title: TEMPRAGEVAL: Temporal RAG Evaluation
covers: temporal questions: as of date X
sources.gap: Directly pressures temporal RAG, so the proposed benchmark must avoid claiming temporal QA novelty and instead focus on explicit stale/current document conflict plus citation snapshot validity.

sources.title: MultiHop-RAG: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multi-Hop Queries
sources.gap: Directly covers multi-hop RAG, so multi-hop synthesis is only defensible as one failure mode inside the broader hard-grounded research taxonomy.

sources.title: MAGIC: A Multi-Hop and Generation-Intensive Chinese Benchmark for LLM Evaluation
sources.gap: Adds another close multi-hop/generation benchmark; the differentiator must be evidence semantics rather than generation difficulty.

sources.title: FaithEval: Can Your Language Model Stay Faithful to Context, Even If "The Moon is Made of Marshmallows"?
sources.gap: Close for context-faithfulness failures, but does not make conclusion-support overreach, source authority, and document lifecycle first-class research QA categories.

category_coverage.differentiator: Must be framed as one slice inside a broader hard-grounded research taxonomy, not as a standalone multi-hop benchmark.
Focus on conflicting document snapshots and explicit stale-evidence rejection rather than generic temporal reasoning or counterfactual context faithfulness.
Document-state changes from appendices, errata, or later sections remain underrepresented in adjacent RAG benchmarks.
Needs to stress cross-format evidence use inside research QA rather than claim novelty over text/table reasoning itself.
Authority hierarchy is distinct from arbitrary contradiction when the benchmark encodes which source controls the conclusion.
Abstention is not novel alone; contribution depends on pairing it with citation-overreach, authority, lifecycle, and temporal constraints.

category_coverage.category: citation supports fact but not conclusion
category_coverage.differentiator: The key distinction is conclusion support, not whether the cited text is real or relevant to a subfact.
Needs adversarial same-name or near-name entities where citations must identify the right referent.

category_coverage.category: temporal questions: as of date X
category_coverage.differentiator: Should be scoped to document snapshot validity and citation dates, not broad temporal QA.
Contradiction is crowded; benchmark value comes from combining contradiction with source authority and research conclusions.

release_gate_instruction: Do not claim novelty until this audit is refreshed after human review completion with final June 2026 source checks and the category-level comparison table is paper-ready.
